definition: The form in which value (abstract labour time) is expressed in exchange. Marx traces four developmental stages: (A) Elementary form (20 yards linen = 1 coat — one commodity expresses its value through another), (B) Total/Expanded form (20 yards linen = 1 coat or 10 lbs tea or...), (C) General form (all commodities express value in one single equivalent), (D) Money form (gold becomes the universal equivalent). The value-form is the economic cell-form of bourgeois society.

contrasts.differential: Value is the substance (abstract labour); the value-form is how that substance appears in exchange relations
Use-value is the natural form of the commodity; the value-form is its social form

definition: The phenomenal form of surplus-value: the difference between the selling price of commodities and their cost-price (c + v). Profit obscures its origin in unpaid labour by appearing to arise from the total capital advanced (constant + variable) rather than from variable capital alone. The rate of profit s/(c+v) is always less than the rate of surplus-value s/v.

contrasts.differential: Surplus-value is the essential relation (unpaid labour); profit is its mystified appearance at the surface of circulation
Profit is the total return on productive capital; interest is the portion accruing to money-capital as such

definition: The ratio of surplus-value to total capital advanced: s/(c+v). The general rate of profit is the average across all branches of production, equalized by competition. Marx argues it has a tendency to fall as the organic composition of capital rises (more constant capital relative to variable capital), though counteracting tendencies (increased exploitation, cheapening of elements of constant capital, etc.) can retard this decline.

contrasts.differential: Rate of surplus-value s/v measures exploitation of labour; rate of profit s/(c+v) measures return on total capital. The latter is always smaller
Rate of profit is the return on productive capital; rate of interest is the price paid for borrowing money-capital

definition: The process by which capital reproduces its conditions of existence: simple reproduction maintains capital at the same scale, expanded reproduction increases it through accumulation. Marx analyzes reproduction of the aggregate social capital (Volume 2, Part 3) in terms of two departments: Department I (means of production) and Department II (means of consumption), showing the conditions for their mutual exchange.

contrasts.differential: Production is the immediate process of creating commodities; reproduction encompasses the full circuit including circulation and the renewal of all conditions
Simple reproduction maintains capital unchanged; accumulation is expanded reproduction where surplus-value is converted back into capital

definition: The sphere in which commodities and money change hands: the metamorphosis of commodities (C-M-C, selling to buy) and the circulation of capital (M-C-M', buying to sell at a profit). Circulation does not create value — value is created in production — but it is the necessary form in which value realizes itself. Volume 2 is subtitled 'The Process of Circulation of Capital.'

contrasts.differential: Production creates value through labour; circulation merely transfers and realizes value already created
Exchange is the individual act of trading; circulation is the total social process of commodity and money movement

definition: The general formula of capital: Money (M) is advanced to purchase commodities (C) — means of production and labour-power — which are productively consumed, and the resulting commodities are sold for more money (M' = M + ΔM). The increment ΔM is surplus-value. This circuit is the defining motion of capital as self-valorizing value, distinguishing it from simple commodity circulation (C-M-C).

contrasts.differential: C-M-C is selling to buy (use-value is the end); M-C-M' is buying to sell at a profit (exchange-value/surplus-value is the end)
Simple circulation serves consumption; capitalist circulation serves the expansion of value

definition: The theoretical problem of how values (determined by socially necessary labour time) are transformed into prices of production (cost-price plus average profit). Because different branches of production have different organic compositions of capital, equal capitals produce unequal amounts of surplus-value. Competition equalizes profit rates, so commodities sell at prices of production that deviate from their values — but total prices equal total values and total profits equal total surplus-value.

contrasts.differential: Value is determined by labour time; prices of production deviate from values to equalize profit rates across industries
Price of production = cost-price + average profit; it differs from value for any individual commodity but aggregates are equal

definition: The ratio of constant capital (c, means of production) to variable capital (v, labour-power), reflecting the technical relation between dead and living labour. Expressed as c/v or as a proportion like 80c + 20v. Higher organic composition means more capital-intensive production. The tendency of rising organic composition drives the tendency of the rate of profit to fall.

contrasts.differential: Technical composition is the physical ratio of means of production to labour; organic composition is this ratio expressed in value terms
Value composition is the ratio c/v at current prices; organic composition is the value composition insofar as it reflects the technical composition

definition: The cyclic movement of capital through its three forms: money capital (M), productive capital (P), and commodity capital (C'). Marx identifies three circuits corresponding to each starting point: the circuit of money capital (M-C...P...C'-M'), the circuit of productive capital (P...C'-M'-C...P), and the circuit of commodity capital (C'-M'-C...P...C'). The total circuit is the unity of all three.

contrasts.differential: The circuit describes the qualitative metamorphoses of capital; turnover measures the time required to complete these circuits
M-C-M' is the general formula; the circuit of capital is its detailed unfolding through production and circulation phases

definition: The mystification whereby social relations between people appear as natural properties of things and relations between things. The commodity-form conceals the social character of labour: value appears as an intrinsic property of commodities rather than as crystallized abstract labour. 'A definite social relation between men assumes, in their eyes, the fantastic form of a relation between things.' Marx compares this to religious mystification where products of the brain appear as independent beings.

contrasts.differential: Under fetishism, social relations are opaque, mediated by things; in a transparent society (Marx's example: Robinson Crusoe), the relation between labour and products is direct and visible
As use-value, the commodity is trivially understandable; as bearer of value, it becomes 'a very queer thing, abounding in metaphysical subtleties'

definition: The qualitative utility of a commodity—its capacity to satisfy a human need. A coat keeps warm; use-value is realized in consumption.
The quantitative ratio in which use-values of one kind exchange for those of another. Expresses abstract labor time socially necessary for production.
Labor considered as undifferentiated expenditure of human labor-power, regardless of its particular form. The substance of value.
Labor in its specific, qualitative form (tailoring, weaving). Creates use-values. Contrasts with abstract labor which creates value.
Capital invested in means of production (machinery, raw materials). Transfers its value to the product without creating new value.
Capital invested in labor-power (wages). Called variable because it produces more value than it costs—the source of surplus value.
The ratio of constant to variable capital (c/v). Rising organic composition is the basis of the tendency of the rate of profit to fall.
M-C-M': money buys commodities to sell for more money. The self-valorization of value. Unlike C-M-C (selling to buy), capital has no natural limit.
Surplus value increased by lengthening the working day beyond necessary labor time. The extensive method of exploitation.
Surplus value increased by reducing necessary labor time through productivity gains. The intensive method, characteristic of developed capitalism.
Capital takes over existing labor processes without transforming them. Workers use traditional methods but now work for a capitalist.
Capital transforms the labor process itself through machinery and factory organization. The specifically capitalist mode of production.
As organic composition rises (more machinery, less labor), the rate of profit (s/(c+v)) tends to fall. The fundamental internal contradiction of capitalism.
The pool of unemployed workers created by capitalist accumulation. Keeps wages down through competition and provides labor for periods of expansion.
The form in which products of labor appear in capitalist society. The commodity is the cell-form (Zellenform) of capitalist wealth.
The form of appearance of value: simple (one commodity against another), expanded, general, and money form. The dialectical development of the commodity.
